question: kit/07-QUALITY-BAR.md, R2, word for word
note: Each vote is one fresh agent that received one picture and the question of R2 and nothing else. The pictures carry neutral names; which judged frame each is stands in the key file, added when every answer is in. Each juror sent its one line to a clerk agent that saved it unchanged; the lines are read from those files by a script.

votes.why: the same fine-grained rock texture repeats across the giant formations.

alien coastline with curved rock arches and creatures is well composed but has flat water shading and repetitive procedural-looking rock and seaweed textures, more like a strong standalone CG render than film-grade work
the mix of detailed wet-ground PBR reflections with stiff repeated alien bird models and visibly procedural rock and cliff textures
The same horizontal rock texture stretches across every curved spire without following its shape.

the alien scene is detailed and coherent, with atmospheric haze, believable wet-sand reflections, and many creatures at different distances, which looks like big-budget film or game-cinematic work, though the repeated rocks and flat wet-sand texture leave some doubt (c).
the conspicuously faceted silhouettes of the foreground rocks.
polished fantastical CG scene (detailed kelp/creature) but simple, plain-shaded foreground rocks and generic fog suggest a strong individual/stock render rather than a top-budget film frame
the faceted foreground rocks meeting a flat reflective water plane without realistic foam or shore interaction and the glossy ribbon-like seaweed
the foreground tendrils have a uniformly glossy, plastic-like surface.
the detailed carcass, wet kelp-like textures, and atmospheric depth with shallow depth of field read as high-end film or cinematic concept-level work.
the repeated creature models have a uniformly embossed skin texture that makes them look like 3D assets.
well-made but plainly CG speculative-creature scene (uniform procedural rock/skin textures, flat clean water reflections) that reads as a polished hobbyist/stock render rather than film-grade VFX
the simple water droplets and flat reflections around the cloned creatures look like a standard 3D render rather than top-budget film VFX.
The foreground creature’s skin has the same dry, sculpted-clay texture from its belly to its legs.
the detailed creature skin, the water reflections and ripples, and the atmospheric depth look like film-quality rendering.
the same perched creature pose repeats conspicuously across the cliff.
repetitive instanced creature copies and tiled/procedural cliff texturing with flat lighting look like a hobbyist/stock 3D render rather than film-grade work.
flat overcast lighting and repetitive instanced creature models with weak contact shadows on the procedural rock ledges
the same curled-neck creature pose repeats across the cliff like copies of a single 3D model.

The thing that most influenced my answer: the rock faces have a stretched, repeating streaky texture and the many winged creatures look like duplicated instances with muddy anatomy. That reads as a competent but unpolished CG render, not a film-grade frame. It is also detailed enough that I doubt it is a web demo (d).
The foreground creatures have stiff, angular wings and flat shading that make them look like simple 3D models.
the low-detail untextured pterosaur models and smeared procedural rock textures that look like a hobbyist Blender render rather than film-grade work
the crude faceted low-poly creature models with stick-like legs and pleated wings
the winged creatures have flat, angular wings that look like folded paper.
the wave spray and atmosphere look film-grade, but the flat, simple pterosaur models and the smeared, repeating rock textures read as a good ordinary 3D render rather than top-budget work.
